note: 拟真样例数据：北京农业贸易 × 新加坡食品加工 非转基因大豆 CIF 新加坡。完整单据链：合同→发票→箱单→订舱→eBL(TradeGo)→保险→融资(HSBC)。所有公司、人名、船名、单号均为虚构。

bill_of_lading.consignee: TO ORDER OF HSBC HONG KONG
bill_of_lading.notify_party: Singapore Food Processing Pte. Ltd., 80 Robinson Road, Singapore
bill_of_lading.cargo: Non-GMO Soybeans (非转基因大豆), Bulk

commercial_invoice.payment_terms: Irrevocable Letter of Credit at Sight
commercial_invoice.pricing_basis: CBOT Soybean Futures (July 2026 contract) + CIF Singapore premium

cargo.grade: Non-GMO Soybeans, Grade No.1, Protein ≥ 38%, Moisture ≤ 13.5%

insurance.policy_type: Institute Cargo Clauses (A) — All Risks, General Average, Theft, Fire, Collision, Total Loss

trade_economics.note: Exporter sourced Non-GMO soybeans from Heilongjiang at ~USD 440/MT (farm-gate + inland logistics to Shanghai). CIF Singapore invoice at USD 520/MT yields ~15.4% gross margin. Verified profit (= invoice 2,600,000 - COGS 2,200,000 = 400,000) funds the RWA discount. Non-GMO premium over conventional soybeans is ~USD 30-40/MT.

financing.repayment_source: Importer Payment under L/C at Sight
financing.security_enforcement: Bank may exercise control over eBL and dispose of cargo upon default event.
financing.note: HSBC Hong Kong provides 80% advance against eBL + Insurance + L/C proceeds. SOFR + 3% for 45 days. Non-GMO premium-grade soybeans with strong buyer (Singapore Food Processing) and bank-intermediated L/C payment — high-quality collateral.

shipment_events.description: 5,000 MT Non-GMO soybeans loaded on board MV Pacific Horizon at Shanghai Port. 4 holds filled, bulk carrier.
eBL TG-EBL-2026-0001 transferred from Beijing Agricultural Trading → HSBC Hong Kong (pledged as collateral under TF-2026-001).
MV Pacific Horizon underway in East China Sea, ETA Singapore May 24. Weather forecast clear.

macro_risk_events.description: CBOT soybean futures near USD 480/MT on South American crop downgrades (Brazil drought reduced safrinha output). US-China Phase One trade deal in focus as 2026 planting season begins. Non-GMO premium stable at ~USD 35/MT.
May is pre-monsoon season for the South China Sea route. Sea state calm, no typhoon activity forecast. Shanghai-Singapore is a 6-day transit — minimal voyage risk.

Buyer Singapore Food Processing is a well-established ASEAN agri-processor with confirmed L/C from HSBC. Seller Beijing Agricultural Trading is a major PRC grain exporter — both counterparties are investment-grade.
